title: Range queries over native histograms mis-count samples against MaxSamples, so the per-query sample limit is enforced ...

source.license_note: Real upstream prometheus PR #18928; ACBench task derived from its regression test + fix.

task.summary: Range queries over native histograms mis-count samples against MaxSamples, so the per-query sample limit is enforced incorrectly.
task.instructions: Fix the defect in the promql package so the failing regression test passes without modifying any test.
task.acceptance_notes: FAIL_TO_PASS must pass; do not edit *_test.go.

code_fault.description: In matrixIterSlice, the histogram sample-size adjustment is computed on the already-resliced (kept) buffer instead of the dropped points, corrupting ev.currentSamples accounting for native histograms.

ops_fault.description: Range/subquery evaluations over native histograms report the wrong number of processed samples, causing MaxSamples limit enforcement to be incorrect.
detection_keywords: query rejected or accepted at wrong threshold
native histogram range query miscounts samples
localization_keywords: histogram buffer rotation around drop index
totalHPointSize called on resliced histograms instead of dropped points
HPoint sample-size accounting for dropped points before mint
kept points size used where dropped size needed
repair_keywords: subtract the dropped points' size from ev.currentSamples
account for the dropped histogram points, not the retained ones

visible_context.issue_text: Range and subquery evaluations over native histograms enforce the per-query MaxSamples limit incorrectly, accepting or rejecting queries at the wrong sample threshold.
error_logs: query processing would load too many samples into memory in query execution
promql: expected MaxSamples=91 to be respected, but sample accounting diverged
currentSamples underflow/drift while evaluating max_over_time over native histograms
